headline: The unwind changed continents again: Brazil repriced in a single session — real -6.4%, EWZ -19.8% — while US semis ripped ~3% into Wednesday's Fed.
summary: Brazil is the new fault line. USD/BRL jumped 6.4% in one day to 5.3716 (z=1.02, 68th percentile), Bovespa fell 13.9% to 176,610 and EWZ lost 19.8% — the single largest one-day move anywhere on the board, in the market that was a bull market in yesterday's note (EWZ had been +14% on the month). Argentina went with it, ARGT -4.9% and at the 0th percentile of its year. This is now a two-front EM accident: Korea is still broken (KOSPI -21.6% on the month at z=-3.0, EWY -18.4%, acceleration -1.81) and the relative trade is in freefall — EEM/SPY z=-2.05 with acceleration -1.57, sitting in the 13th percentile. Note what did NOT break: USD/MXN fell 0.9% today and Mexico's IPC is +6.9% on the month at z=1.44, USD/KRW is at the 0.4 percentile, USD/CNY at the 0th. There is no generalized dollar squeeze — DXY is +0.2%. This is idiosyncratic sovereign repricing, which means it is tradable as dispersion rather than hedgeable as beta.

Against that, the US tape did the opposite of yesterday. The chips that led the global unwind bounced hardest: SOXX +2.9%, SMH +2.7%, MU +3.0%, AMD +2.8%, NVDA +2.4%, AVGO +2.3%, with SMH/SPY +2.0% on the day off a 1-month z of -1.45 and SMH still 4.8% above its 200-day. NDX +1.1%, SPX +0.7% to 7,676.8 and back in the 90th percentile. Volatility came in: VIX -5.5% to 18.39, VIX3M -2.6%, and the term structure backed off to 0.922 (-2.9%), with SKEW -6.7% on the week. The rates picture is the quiet bull case: levels are still ugly (10y exactly 5.00%, 5y 4.84%, 30y 5.31%) but every acceleration z-score is deeply negative — 2y -2.06, 5y -1.98, 10y -1.92, 10y real -1.97 — and the month's changes are -13bp, -14bp, -17bp, -18bp. TLT is +3.4% on the month with acceleration +1.37, IEF +1.6% with the highest acceleration in the credit block at +1.70, and MOVE slipped to 102.19. The tightening impulse is decelerating into Wednesday's FOMC even as the levels stay punitive.

Underneath the index, the de-risking has not stopped — it just rotated. High-beta/low-vol is -14.9% on the month at z=-2.39 with acceleration -2.55; growth/value sits at the 6th percentile of its year; discretionary/staples at the 6th; industrials/utilities z=-2.08. The defensive bid is the thing accelerating: XLP +7.2% on the month (z=1.83, acceleration 2.07), SPLV acceleration 2.39, USMV at the 99th percentile, WMT +11.4% and COST +8.9% on the month. That is not a tape that believes in the bounce it just had. Comm services is the clean short: XLC -1.6% on a +0.7% S&P day, -8.1% on the month, 0th percentile of its year, with META -16.1% on the month at acceleration -2.95, NFLX -10.2% and also 0th percentile, GOOGL -8.0% on the week. The AI-power complex keeps bleeding regardless of the chip bounce: REMX -22.4% on the month, NLR -13.9% and 1st percentile, uranium -16.0%, GRID -9.2%, ETN -15.5% at z=-2.29, GEV -10.7%. Credit is soft but not cracking: HYG/IEF -2.0% on the month at z=-1.5 while HYG sits in the 40th percentile against an S&P in the 90th.

The inflation constraint is loosening at the margin and that is what the Fed has to price. RBOB is -7.9% on the month at z=-0.85 and -2.7% today, WTI -1.9% to 101.34 and Brent 110.24 — but crude is still 18.3% above its 200-day and +76.5% YTD, 5-year breakevens are 2.47% (+13bp on the month, turning up), and the 30-year mortgage is pinned at 7.32%, +37bp on the month and the 94th percentile of the year. The inflation composite is -47, the rates composite -42. Energy equity remains the single best-paid expression of that: XLE +12.2% on the month at the 100th percentile with RS +13.1%, XOP +12.9%, XOM +14.9% (z=1.55), CVX +13.5%. Copper +1.2% with copper/gold at the 100th percentile and DBC at the 97th says the growth pulse (composite -6) is not the problem. The problem is the price of risk: risk regime -22, breadth composite -25, and a market where equal-weight/cap-weight carries the highest acceleration on the board (+3.18) precisely because the leadership keeps getting liquidated.

good.text: The tightening impulse is decelerating across the whole curve even with 10s at exactly 5.00%: 2y -13bp, 5y -14bp, 10y -17bp, 30y -18bp on the month, with acceleration z-scores of -2.06, -1.98, -1.92 and -1.50. The 10-year real yield is 2.66%, -17bp on the month at acceleration -1.97, and MOVE eased to 102.19.

Semis took the first real upside day since the Korea unwind began: SOXX +2.9%, SMH +2.7%, MU +3.0%, AMD +2.8%, NVDA +2.4%, TSM +1.4%, with SMH/SPY +2.0% off a 1-month z of -1.45 and SMH still 4.8% above its 200-day.
Volatility exhaled into the Fed: VIX -5.5% to 18.39, VIX3M -2.6%, the VIX/VIX3M term structure back to 0.922 (-2.9%) and SKEW -6.7% on the week. The panic bid in short-dated protection is draining.

Rate-sensitive domestics are bidding the yield relief: KRE +5.0% and KBE +4.8% on the week, ITB +5.8%, XHB +4.1%, XLRE +2.7%, with equal-weight/cap-weight breadth carrying the highest acceleration in the entire digest at +3.18.

Energy remains the only sector with trend, relative strength and cash flow all aligned: XLE +12.2% on the month at the 100th percentile (RS +13.1%), XOP +12.9%, XOM +14.9% at z=1.55 and the 100th percentile, CVX +13.5%.
The cycle pulse is not endorsing recession: copper +1.2%, copper/gold at the 100th percentile of its year, DBC at the 97th, Dow Transports +2.6% on the week and FDX +5.2% on the month.

bad.text: Brazil blew up in one session: USD/BRL +6.4% to 5.3716, Bovespa -13.9%, EWZ -19.8% — the largest single-day move on the board, in a market that was leading EM a week ago. Argentina followed, ARGT -4.9% at the 0th percentile.

EM as an asset class is now failing on two fronts: EEM/SPY at z=-2.05 and the 13th percentile, EEM -9.1% on the month at z=-1.95, KOSPI -21.6% on the month at z=-3.0 and EWY -18.4%, with the EM currency basket -0.8% on the week.

The de-risking under the index is accelerating, not fading: high-beta/low-vol -14.9% on the month at z=-2.39 with acceleration -2.55, growth/value at the 6th percentile, discretionary/staples at the 6th, industrials/utilities z=-2.08, min-vol at the 99th percentile. Defensive leadership accelerating is bad news dressed as strength.

Comm services is the only group printing 52-week lows while the S&P sits in the 90th percentile: XLC -1.6% today, -8.1% on the month, 0th percentile; META -16.1% on the month at acceleration -2.95; NFLX -10.2% and also 0th percentile; GOOGL -8.0% on the week.

The AI-power and materials-input complex keeps liquidating through the chip bounce: REMX -22.4% on the month, NLR -13.9% at the 1st percentile, uranium -16.0%, GRID -9.2%, ETN -15.5% at z=-2.29, GEV -10.7%, COPX -14.9%.

The inflation constraint is still binding into the FOMC: 5-year breakevens 2.47% (+13bp on the month, turning up), 30-year mortgage 7.32% at the 94th percentile and +37bp on the month, WTI still +76.5% YTD and 18.3% above its 200-day. Credit quietly lags — HYG/IEF -2.0% on the month at z=-1.5 with HYG in the 40th percentile.

trades.name: Mexico over Brazil
trades.line: Long EWW vs short EWZ — LatAm dispersion, not LatAm beta
trades.expr: Equal dollar long EWW / short EWZ, 1% NAV per leg. FX overlay version: long MXN / short BRL 3-month forwards.
trades.thesis: Today was sovereign repricing, not a dollar squeeze — DXY was +0.2% and USD/KRW and USD/CNY sit at the 0th percentile. A 6.4% one-day currency gap and a 13.9% index drop almost never resolve in a session; positioning unwinds take weeks. Mexico is doing the exact opposite on the same continent.
trades.trigger: USD/BRL +6.4% to 5.3716 and EWZ -19.8% in one day, versus USD/MXN -0.9% today after a +4.6% month and MXX +6.9% on the month at z=1.44 with acceleration +1.40.
trades.stop: EWZ recovers more than half of today's drop, or USD/BRL trades back below 5.10 — that would make this a liquidity air-pocket, not a regime change.
trades.target: 15% on the pair over three months; EWW/EWZ back to its 3-month relative highs.

trades.name: Semis washout bounce
trades.line: Long SMH: -14% month, trend intact, first upside acceleration
trades.expr: Buy SMH outright, or December upside calls ~10% OTM for 50bp premium; beta-neutral version shorts SPY against it.
trades.thesis: The Korea/memory unwind drove SOXX -14.1% and SMH -10.7% on the month to a 1-month z of -1.69/-1.45 without breaking the uptrend — SMH is still 4.8% above its 200-day. When a liquidation stops being fed offshore, the snapback in the most-shorted leadership is violent.
trades.trigger: SMH +2.7% and SOXX +2.9% today, MU +3.0%, AMD +2.8%, NVDA +2.4%, TSM +1.4%, with SMH/SPY +2.0% on the day after a -10.0% month of relative strength.
trades.stop: SMH closes below its 200-day near 517, or SMH/SPY takes out today's lows — that would mean the unwind has a second leg.
trades.target: SMH 600 (+11%), closing half the 1-month relative gap versus SPY.

trades.name: Belly of the curve into the FOMC
trades.line: Long IEF / 5y futures — levels high, acceleration deeply negative
trades.expr: Buy IEF, or long FV (5-year note) futures. To isolate the belly, fund by shorting TLT dollar-for-dollar at half size.
trades.thesis: Yields are near the highs of the year but the second derivative has rolled everywhere — the market is already discounting a decelerating tightening impulse, and the belly is where a cut gets paid without taking term-premium or breakeven risk.
trades.trigger: 2y 4.68% (-13bp on the month, acceleration -2.06), 5y 4.84% (-14bp, -1.98), 10y real 2.66% (-17bp, -1.97); IEF's +1.70 acceleration is the highest reading in the credit block and MOVE slipped to 102.19.
trades.stop: 10y closes above 5.15%, or 5-year breakevens break 2.60% from today's 2.47% — that makes this an inflation problem the Fed cannot ease into.

trades.name: Short crude on the product crack
trades.line: Short WTI: gasoline -7.9% on the month is leading crude lower
trades.expr: Short front-month WTI futures, or buy December $95 puts for ~50bp premium. Keep XLE long as a partial offset if you own energy equity.
trades.thesis: Refined products turn before crude. Crude is 18.3% above its 200-day and +76.5% YTD on an inflation bid, and it is the single input keeping the rates composite at -42 and the inflation composite at -47. Breaking it is the cheapest way to get everything else easier.
trades.trigger: RBOB -2.7% today and -7.9% on the month at z=-0.85, WTI -1.9% to 101.34, Brent -5.6%, DBC -0.9% — crude's own acceleration has rolled to -0.15 and Brent's to -0.85.
trades.stop: WTI closes above $105 (new cycle high), or gasoline reclaims its 1-month high — then the supply story is real and this is a loser.
trades.target: WTI $90, roughly a -11% move and the 200-day premium halved.

trades.name: Sell the discretionary bounce
trades.line: Long XLP vs short XLY — fade today's +1.4% ratio pop
trades.expr: Long XLP / short XLY, equal dollars, 1.5% NAV per leg. Single-name version: long WMT and COST versus short XLY.
trades.thesis: The defensive bid is the fastest-accelerating thing in the US tape while the index grinds sideways. XLY/XLP sits at the 6th percentile of its year in a confirmed downtrend; a 1.4% one-day bounce in a ratio that deep in a downtrend is an entry, not a turn.
trades.trigger: XLP +7.2% on the month at z=1.83 with acceleration +2.07, SPLV acceleration +2.39, USMV at the 99th percentile, while high-beta/low-vol is -14.9% on the month at acceleration -2.55 and XLY/XLP bounced +1.4% today.
trades.stop: XLY/XLP reclaims 1.35 (+4% from 1.299), or SPHB/SPLV turns up through a positive 1-month z — that means the risk appetite is genuinely rebuilding.
trades.target: XLY/XLP to 1.22, about 6% on the pair.

trades.name: Short comm services
trades.expr: Short XLC, or buy November META puts ~5% OTM; pair against long SPY to strip out index beta.
trades.thesis: Comm services is the only sector making 52-week lows while the S&P sits in the 90th percentile — the market is repricing ad and streaming economics against AI capex, and that is a multi-quarter de-rating, not a dip.
trades.trigger: XLC -1.6% on a day the S&P was +0.7%, -5.7% on the week, -8.1% on the month, 0th percentile, RS -7.3%; META -16.1% on the month at acceleration -2.95, NFLX -10.2% and also 0th percentile, GOOGL -8.0% on the week.
trades.stop: XLC rallies 5% from 103.85 or reclaims its 200-day (currently 7.8% above spot).
trades.target: XLC toward 95, another -8%; -10% versus SPY on the beta-neutral version.
